title: A parametric Keldysh decomposition
summary: Contour integral algorithms seek to compute a small number of eigenvalues located within a bounded region of the complex plane. These methods can be applied to both linear and nonlinear matrix eigenvalue problems. In the latter case, the foundation of these methods comes from the Keldysh decomposition, which breaks the nonlinear matrix-valued function into two parts: a rational function whose poles match the desired eigenvalues, and a remainder term that is analytic within the target region.
